description: The bar chart, titled “Runtime Comparison of Models in Streaming Environment,” visually compares the inference runtime (in seconds) of five different models under a streaming setup. The vertical y-axis represents “Runtime (seconds)” and spans from 0 to 400, with major gridlines at intervals of 50. The horizontal x-axis lists five models: “Our Joint Framework,” “ChatGPT,” “DeepSeek,” “LLaMA,” and “Claude.” A legend in the upper-left corner indicates that “Our Joint Framework” is represented by a dark green bar, while all other models (“LLM Models”) are shown in light blue. The chart shows that “Our Joint Framework” achieves a runtime of 77 seconds — significantly lower than all LLMs. Among the LLMs, “DeepSeek” is the slowest at 365 seconds, followed by “Claude” at 244 seconds (inferred from bar height, though unlabeled), “ChatGPT” at 190 seconds, and “LLaMA” at 172 seconds. The bars are not sorted by runtime, but the stark contrast in height between the green bar and the blue bars emphasizes the efficiency of the proposed joint framework. The chart visually supports the paper’s claim that integrating LLMs into a joint framework can substantially reduce runtime in streaming conversational environments compared to standalone LLM inference.
